correctness.rationale: Reconstruction uses the exact color count for a blade vertex of color gamma: a_beta + 1[beta=center] - 1[beta=gamma]. With m=2 its two neighbors must differ and the center alone imposes each leaf-color total <=n. With m>=3 a monochromatic blade fails, so the exact local occupancy caps are center<=floor(m/2)-1 and other<=floor(m/2). These caps force the center automatically because n floor(m/2)<=floor(nm/2). The q-palette count is a product of independent blade multinomial sums and the center-color choice; m=2 instead has an exact capacitated multinomial sum. The explicit optimal constructions prove 3 colors except the m=3 capacity obstruction requiring 4. An independent adjacency-based checker corroborates the criterion and all labeled-map counts in 35 finite parameter-palette cases and 1,560 wider constructions.

originality.rationale: The founding primary source treats strong-majority vertex coloring and complete graphs but does not include the generalized windmill or the structural counting formula in its inspected full text. Searches for friendship, windmill, bouquet and join-of-cliques formulations found only different-invariant graph results or strong-majority edge coloring. A published majority C friendship result concerns the opposite per-vertex inequality and maximum rather than minimum number of colors, hence does not imply the new statement. The complete-graph one-blade scalar case is credited as prior and excluded from the new domain.

value.rationale: The result is an all-parameter exact classification of a canonical block graph family for a newly introduced invariant. It exhibits a nonobvious threshold unique to 3-clique blades and proves an exact local-global decoupling for every larger blade, while 2-clique blades retain a global balancing coupling at the center. The factorization gives all palette-map counts as a power of a truncated exponential coefficient and yields explicit infinite optimal-color enumerations, rather than a routine small graph or a scalar bound.
